headline: South Asia: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance.
- Africa: Sudan: UN Condemns Deadly Drone Strikes On Sudan Civilians.
- Western Russia: One killed and one injured in Russian attacks on Chernihiv.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army support for Golden Dome missile shield takes shape.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: US Army support for Golden Dome missile shield takes shape.
A U.S. Army air defense unit has been "earmarked" for support of the Golden Dome for America project, an Army official confirmed.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: Marine Corps creates first medium missile battalion.
As the service's first medium missile battalion, the 1st Battalion, 10th Marine Regiment, will be equipped with NMESIS as a complement to its artillery.
The Caribbean - bottom line: THIRSTY FOR CASH - NWC seeks massive rate hike, warns of investment cuts without it as debts mount.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: THIRSTY FOR CASH - NWC seeks massive rate hike, warns of investment cuts without it as debts mount.
The Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR) has confirmed that it received an application from the National Water Commission (NWC) for a 51 per cent increase in tariff over a five-year period. The NWC’s senior management told a meeting of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) at Gordon House on Tuesday that the utility had applied to the regulatory body last Friday, putting its approximately 500,000 customers on notice. In a release yesterday, the OUR said the tariff application covers the period 2026-27 to 2030-31.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: One killed and one injured in Russian attacks on Chernihiv.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: One killed and one injured in Russian attacks on Chernihiv.
Dmytro Bryzhynskyi has reported that a repeat Russian drone strike killed one person and injured another at a commercial business in Chernihiv.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian forces strike university in Kremenchuk: three injured, including teenager – photos.
A Russian drone hit a university building in Poltava Oblast, injuring a 16-year-old and two other people. Separate strikes sparked fires at on office building and a warehouse in Poltava.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: "She should have lived and created the future of Ukraine": Mariana Tokarchuk, 21, killed in Kyiv attack.
Mariana Tokarchuk’s funeral will be held in her home village of Derazhne, her local hromada has announced. She was killed in a Russian missile attack on Kyiv.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Axios: Trump's envoy Kushner pressed Ukraine to stop strikes on Russian oil refineries during Oslo talks.
US President Donald Trump's son-in-law and special envoy Jared Kushner, who joined talks in Oslo remotely on 20 October, reiterated Trump's demand that Ukraine stop attacking Russian oil refineries, Axios reports.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Russia energy sanctions will stay despite US diesel deal, von der Leyen says.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Russia energy sanctions will stay despite US diesel deal, von der Leyen says.
The Commission president warned that “Russia is not a trusted supplier of energy."
- Politico Europe, just now: Suspicious drones spotted flying over French military sites.
An investigation was opened after drones were spotted above a naval base in Toulon.

AFRICA

[Dabanga] Khartoum -- The United Nations has condemned drone attacks that have killed at least 48 civilians in Blue Nile and West Kordofan, including women and children sheltering after fleeing their homes, and called for accountability and respect for international humanitarian law.
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: Russia: Huge flames and smoke rise over St Petersburg after drone strikes.
Huge plumes of black smoke billowed over St Petersburg, Russia’s second-largest city, on Sunday, 18 October, as a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack sparked fires at industrial and logistics facilities. Russian officials said 126 drones had been intercepted in the surrounding region.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 4 hours ago: Nigeria: In Eight Days, Precision Military Air Strikes Kill 103 Terrorists.
[This Day] Abuja -- The Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), has sustained intelligence-led precision air strikes against Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists across its joint operations area, neutralising a total of 103 terrorists and destroying several logistics hubs and storage facilities between 10 and 18 October 2026.
- Africanews, one hour ago: Woman, 65, killed in shark attack at South African beach.
A 65-year-old woman has died after being attacked by a shark while swimming at a popular beach in South Africa's Eastern Cape province.

- Jerusalem Post, 16 hours ago: IDF kills Hamas terrorist involved in October 7 abduction of Shani Louk.

Abuse, threats against Australian lawmakers are rising in a country where political violence has historically been rare.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: Mozambique: Peace Day Speeches Show History Forgotten and Lessons Not Learned.
[Mozambique News Reports And Clippings] The day of Peace and Reconciliation (4 October) marked the anniversary of the signing of a peace accord in Rome by the Mozambique government and Renamo rebels in 1992, that ended a brutal decade-long war. After years of Frelimo saying ''we do not talk to terrorists'', it did just that in Rome. And the settlement involved Renamo becoming the official opposition, with some guerrilla fighters becoming members of parliament.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one hour ago: Mozambique: Another Leader of Mondlane's Party Killed.
[Mozambique News Reports And Clippings] Araújo Tendence, a senior member of Anamola in Mopeia, Zambézia, was shot dead Friday (9 Oct) evening at his home. Anamola (National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique) is the political party led by Mondlane, and founded in August 2025. Since then, Mondlane says that almost 60 members have been killed, with no investigations of the murders. - AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Court Overturns U.S.$36,000 Equipment Judgment Over Defective Service, Unsupported Damages.
[New Zimbabwe] The High Court has overturned a default judgment against businessman Lloyd Vernon Mina over disputed excavator and truck deals after finding that court papers were improperly served and damages were awarded without evidence proving the losses.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Teachers Slam Zanu-PF Over Resolution to Influence Government Job Recruitment.
[New Zimbabwe] TEACHERS have condemned a ZANU PF conference resolution proposing that the ruling party recommend candidates for government jobs, warning that it threatens the constitutional separation between the State and the party.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance.
ISLAMABAD: Adviser to the National Command Authority retired Lt Gen Khalid Kidwai on Tuesday warned that Pakistan could review its deployment options to restore strategic balance in South Asia, saying India was moving towards a more prepared, potentially first-use capable nuclear posture. “Pakistan never has and never will accept strategic imbalances to be induced in South Asia,” Mr Kidwai said at the second Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference, hosted by the Strategic Vision Institute, an Islamabad based think tank specialising in strategic issues.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Jerusalem Post, The Hindu - International, Ukrainska Pravda, Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: US envoy to meet Putin after 'positive' talks with Zelensky.
Washington’s envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Saint Petersburg early Wednesday to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin following what US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described as “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine. The trip by President Donald Trump’s special envoy is part of efforts to draw a line under a bitter feud between him and Zelensky over the war with Russia. After talks with Witkoff in Oslo, Zelensky thanked Washington on Tuesday for the resumption of US intelligence sharing on Russian strikes.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Makkah alliance binds partners to decade-long pact.

- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: CDF Munir-Pezeshkian meeting raises peace hopes.
ISLAMABAD: Iranian leaders have told Pakistan that the United States must take the first steps to rebuild trust, and that the acceptance of Tehran’s seven-point proposal could provide a starting point for renewed negotiations. The message was conveyed during Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s visit on Tuesday, where he met with President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Mohsen Rezaei, a representative of Iran’s supreme leader and secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.
India - bottom line: Woman who revived boyfriend twice after lightning strike to get bravery award.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Woman who revived boyfriend twice after lightning strike to get bravery award.
During a hiking trip, Eva Broderick's quick thinking saved her boyfriend Nick's life after they were both struck by lightning. Stranded in an isolated area, they faced delays as rescuers searched for them without precise location data. After their recovery, Nick's heartfelt proposal led to their wedding nearly a year later in August. Eva's heroic actions highlight the life-saving potential of CPR knowledge in unpredictable outdoor situations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: India moves to develop its first indigenous aviation gun for Prachand, Rudra helicopters.
India's Defence Research and Development Organisation has shortlisted two domestic firms for developing an indigenous 20mm aviation gun. This initiative aims to increase indigenous content in the Light Combat Helicopter Prachand and Rudra helicopters. The development is expected to take around two years before production orders are distributed based on cost calculations. Additionally, efforts are ongoing to indigenise the helicopters' other weapon systems, including anti-tank guided missiles.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: World On Track For 2.6 Degrees Celsius Warming This Century: UN.
Even if countries deliver their latest climate pledges in full, global temperatures could still rise 2.6C above pre-industrial levels by 2100, said the annual Emissions Gap Report.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Missouri court overturns ruling giving couple ownership of neighbour's road.
In a notable case from Missouri, a couple gained legal rights to their isolated property via their neighbor's land. Although the court initially granted them ownership of the access road, it later corrected this decision. Ultimately, they received a permanent easement, illustrating the difference between property rights and ownership. The couple can access their property while the neighbor retains the land under the road.

China’s Type 051C destroyer Shenyang has been spotted undergoing sea trials after a reported refit, as the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) begins phasing out legacy warships following the commissioning of a massive wave of new vessels. Witness photographs circulating on social media appear to show the Shenyang, hull number 115 and lead ship of the Type 051C class, with its Russian-made hardware replaced by domestic air defence systems. Singapore has warned it will go after companies responsible for the forest fires in Indonesia causing the regional haze, but cross-border challenges remain stumbling blocks to solving a problem that has plagued the city state for decades. Analysts point to long-standing obstacles hampering the country’s decade-old haze legislation, such as complex corporate ownership and opaque transboundary supply chains. To date, no company has been prosecuted under the law. Beyond legal threats, greater...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: AFP charging almost one person a week for targeting politicians, says commissioner - video.
- The Guardian - Australia, 11 hours ago: AFP charging almost one person a week for targeting politicians, says commissioner - video.
The Australian federal police commissioner, Krissy Barrett, says police are ‘charging almost one individual every week for targeting commonwealth parliamentarians or high office holders’. Speaking at a joint press conference with Victoria police on the investigation into Monday afternoon’s attack on the Indi MP, Helen Haines, Barrett says people who make online threats against parliamentarians are often ‘absolutely shocked’ when officers show up at their door to execute a search warrant or lay charges.

Certainly, it’s a reminder that the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago.
- The Guardian - Australia, 12 hours ago: My late wife Jo Cox was murdered in her constituency in 2016. The alleged attack on Helen Haines is a punch to the gut | Brendan Cox.
Moments like these can reinforce our divisions or remind us of what we stand to lose when hatred and intimidation are allowed to brutalise our democracy It’s never a good sign when you turn on your phone to find a dozen messages asking if you are OK. For reasons you will come to understand, I only get those messages when something awful has happened. So on Monday, when I came out of an all-day meeting on antisemitism and picked up the messages from friends, I clicked across to check the news with real dread.
